newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov oil demand up 1.3 pct from last year - API.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov oil demand up 1.3 pct from last year - API.

text.p: U.S. deliveries of petroleum products were up 1.3 percent in November from a year ago, pushed mostly by a 6.2 percent jump in distillate deliveries, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
Petroleum deliveries, a key measure of demand, averaged 18.22 million barrels per day, up from 17.98 million in November 1995, the API said in its monthly summary.

Distillate deliveries averaged 3.44 million bpd in November, up 6.3 percent from a year ago and a recent-year record for November on unusually cold Northeast temperatures and growing commercial truck traffic.
Distillate output in November averaged 3.63 million bpd, up nearly nine percent from a year ago. When combined with October, it set an all-time record for a two-month period, the API said.
Distillate deliveries exceeded likely consumption, it said, and stocks grew to 120.7 million barrels at month's end, up from 117.5 million in October.
Gasoline deliveries averaged 7.79 million bpd, down 1.0 percent from November 1995's 7.87 million, partly because of technical factors and because of higher retail prices.
Gasoline stocks ended the month at 190.3 million barrels, down from 190.8 million in October.
U.S. oil imports in November averaged 7.18 million bpd, down 1.7 percent from a year ago and the lowest level since February.

The API said about 90,000 bpd of the lower imports was offset by additional withdrawals from the government's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, where supplies were drawn down by nearly five percent for the year.
Domestic crude production in November slipped 1.4 percent from a year ago to 6.49 million bpd from 6.59 million bpd, with the decline split roughly in half between Alaska and the lower 48 states.
Refinery operations were at 92.8 percent of capacity, up from 92.1 percent in November 1995.
Stocks of all petroleum products stood at 968.4 million barrels at the end of November, down 1.7 percent from the end of October and down 4.4 percent from a year ago.
In other petroleum products, kerosine jet fuel deliveries were up 1.9 percent at 1.61 million bpd from 1.58 million bpd in November 1995.
Residual fuel oil deliveries averaged 811,000 bpd, up 2.3 percent from November 1995's 793,000 bpd, boosted by an increase in natural gas prices.
Deliveries of other oils rose by 2.1 percent to 4.70 million bpd from 4.60 a year ago, boosted by the cold weather's effects on propane demand.
